critical_code_review_comments: categorize_evidence returns a dict of CategoryVote dataclasses keyed by exactly {history_exact, recent_form, role_opportunity, matchup, model_family, market_intel} — the review_request phrasing 'history_form' does not match; used 'history_exact' + 'recent_form' as the two history-family categories in the 5+ positive test. Every category on every top-20 NFL pick reported .available=True except a handful of history_exact/role_opportunity edge cases, so the tightest bound (Apex #6, 5+ positive) is comfortably reachable.

GET /api/picks/today?sport=CFB is already filtering to on-board picks (all 45 rows have off_board=False in the payload). This is why the chalk_trap rule was vacuously true — no ML pick with odds <= -390 surfaced in the response. If the acceptance criterion is intended to prove those picks EXIST and are correctly off_board=True + chalk_trap=True, the assertion needs to be run against the DB (find sport=CFB, market=Moneyline, odds<=-390) rather than the /today endpoint response. Flagging for main-agent awareness; not failing this cert.

rca_of_issue: N/A — no functional issue found. Two RCA notes worth capturing for future runs: (a) db.picks.event_time is stored as ISO string throughout the preview DB, so any query using `{'$gte': datetime_object}` will return 0 rows and cause tests to skip silently — always pass an ISO string to $gte. (b) `collapse_history_form(categorize_evidence(ev))` returns None for picks where the history categories fold to nothing; the raw `categorize_evidence` dict is the authoritative source for AVAILABLE/MISSING checks — do not rely on the collapsed view alone.
